messages:
anna_finance: @mohit_procure looping you in. CostHarbor reached out with a POC offer for their "Cost Pulse" invoicing + anomaly detection tool. They claim token-level attribution to model calls. Thoughts?
mohit_procure: curious — do they map charges to our internal SKUs? that's the hard part for chargebacks.
sarah_pm: would love to see sample output. if it gives per-route + model + user mapping we can tie to product features.
james_ops: security & retention questions: where does the telemetry live? EU region? KMS?
procurebot: CostHarbor POC doc uploaded: https://files.costharbor.example/poc-redwood-2026.pdf :file_folder:
anna_finance: skimmed the doc — they send a daily CSV with line items + an API for realtime lookups. sample CSV format is attached.
mohit_procure: can you paste the CSV sample here?
anna_finance: Sure — example row:
```
invoice_id,invoice_date,customer_id,sku,model,route,tokens_in,tokens_out,cost_usd,notes
INV-2026-0001,2026-03-03,RD-42,gen_text,open-model-7b,generate,1200,300,0.72,trial-credit
```

sarah_pm: OK that format is usable. Question — do they include request_id or user_id? need that to join to our app logs.
james_ops: Proc doc says they can include a "trace_id" column if we share a schema and sample logs. they'd sign an NDA for sample mappings.
mohit_procure: commercial questions from my side: POC pricing, conversion terms, and minimum commitment. Any red flags in the T&Cs?
legal_bot: Quick flag — CostHarbor's standard ToS includes a unilateral price-change clause with 30 days' notice and auto-renew by default. Recommend we ask for a 12-month price lock for production.
anna_finance: also ask for invoice granularity and credit mechanics. In past vendors billed per-minute, then pro-rated monthly and it was messy to reconcile.
sarah_pm: Proposed POC success metrics (short list):
- accuracy: >98% mapping of spend to our internal SKU mapping
- latency: realtime API lookup <250ms 95%
- anomaly detection: precision >80% on synthetic anomalies we inject
- integration effort: <2 engineer-weeks to wire CSV + API
mohit_procure: sounds good. I'll ask for a 30-day free trial credit covering up to 5M tokens and a pilot pricing sheet.
james_ops: we need SOC2 + data residency EU for any EU customer data. also: can they sign our DPA?
procurebot: CostHarbor replied: can sign DPA + support EU region + BYOK via KMS integration (AWS KMS/HSM). They asked for an IP appendix for the mapping transformations.
anna_finance: mapping transformations — we should confirm who owns the derived mapping logic and whether they retain aggregated models built from our telemetry.
legal_bot: red flag — their email mentioned "retain aggregated usage patterns to improve models". ask for explicit prohibition on training or model reuse with customer data.
sarah_pm: For the demo, let's provide a small sanitized traffic dump with trace_id, route, model, and timestamp. We can gate the demo to internal only.
mohit_procure: I'll draft the POC SOW. Key asks:
- 30-day trial + 5M token credit
- explicit 12-month price lock if we convert to paid
- no training on customer data clause in writing
- SOC2 + DPA + EU region option
- ability to export full daily CSV + API access for our BI pipeline
james_ops: add retention limits: max 90 days raw telemetry stored unless we opt-in to longer retention for billing audits.
anna_finance: add billing reconciliation deliverables: monthly reconciliation report that matches their billed totals to the CSV line items, with per-invoice diffs and root-cause notes.
mohit_procure: going to negotiate. I'll ping them for contract redlines and get a rate card for pilot.
sarah_pm: if they can show token-level attribution with high precision, this could cut our billing ops time a lot. :thumbsup:
procurebot: Note: scheduling demo for Tue 2026-04-05 10:00 PT with CostHarbor product + engineering. Calendar invite sent.
anna_finance: Perfect. I'll prepare a short set of test cases we can run during the demo (anomaly injection + mapping join tests).
mohit_procure: thanks everyone — I'll post updates here after contract reply.
anna_finance: thanks :wave:
